newsitem.title: INDIA: India soybean sowing picks up, slow in some areas.
newsitem.headline: India soybean sowing picks up, slow in some areas.

text.p: Sowing has been completed in nearly 60 percent of the area under soybean in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh but has been affected in some regions due to a lack of rain, state officials and traders said on Friday.
Madhya Pradesh produces 80 percent of the country's soybean output.
The industry has targeted a 5.7 million hectare soybean area nationwide for the 1997/98 (November-October) crop, out of which Madhya Pradesh would account for 4.0 million hectares.
"Soybean crop condition is normal in Indore and Ujjain sub-divisions," said L.P. Patel, a senior official in the state Agriculture Department.
A.D. Majumdar, another official in the Agriculture Department, said 33 districts in the state had received more than normal rains while in 27 districts rainfall was still deficient.
"Farmers and the Agriculture Department are worried about the erratic rains (in some areas)," Majumdar said.

Traders said soybean arrivals in the central Indian markets were about 800 tonnes per day, the same as last year. Farmers were increasingly releasing stocks they had held back in the hope of getting better prices.
Soybean in the domestic markets was quoted at 11,000-11,400 rupees per tonne, compared with about 11,700-12,000 rupees at the same time last year, traders said.
Export demand for soymeal was poor due to low availability. Soymeal for export was quoted at $265-268 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship), the same as last year.
Traders said exporters had contracted about 2.45 million tonnes of soymeal for overseas sales in 1996/97 against 2.6 million tonnes in the previous year.
